models.model_label: Future returns on accrual portfolio rank, consistent-signal indicator and interaction, and controls (Equation 3; Table 4 Panel B)
models.sample_description: Full-sample firm-years from 1981–1996 with Compustat financial statement and CRSP return data and available analyst forecast revisions, subject to the paper’s nonmissing-data, firm-size, and share-price filters. The selected full-control model is estimated in separate annual regressions for return horizons t+1, t+2, and t+3. Table 4 reports the number of annual fits by horizon but not observation N for any fit; other missing controls also make analysis counts vary.
models.method_details: The authors report separate annual regressions but do not name the estimator used for the Table 4 fits; it is left unknown.

dependent_variable.name: R_{t+i}
dependent_variable.definition: Twelve-month size-adjusted buy-and-hold return, including dividends, for horizon i = 1, 2, or 3. Size adjustment subtracts the buy-and-hold return of the firm’s assigned size portfolio. The return window begins at the start of the fourth month after fiscal year-end; size portfolios are formed from NYSE/AMEX firms ranked into deciles by beginning-of-year market value of equity, and sample firms are assigned by their beginning-of-year equity value.
dependent_variable.formula: R_{t+i} = firm 12-month buy-and-hold return including dividends − buy-and-hold return of the assigned size-decile portfolio; i ∈ {1,2,3}.

evidence.quote: Future returns, Rtþi, are twelve-month size-adjusted buy-and-hold returns, inclusive of dividends.
To size-adjust a firm’s return, we subtract from the firm’s buy-and-hold return the buy-and-hold return to its size-matched portfolio.

To calculate this adjustment, we rank all sample firms that are traded on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and American Stock Exchange (AMEX) into 10 portfolios based on market value of equity at the beginning of the year.
We then assign each sample firm to one of the portfolios based on the firm’s market value of equity at the beginning of the year and calculate the buy-and-hold return for each size portfolio.
returns window begins at
As with all of our tests, i ranges from one to three.

independent_variables.name: C
independent_variables.definition: Year-t indicator for consistent accrual and analyst forecast-revision signals about low earnings persistence: one when Accruals_t is negative and the consensus forecast for year t+1 is revised upward around the year-t earnings announcement, or Accruals_t is positive and that forecast is revised downward; zero otherwise. Accruals uses the paper’s total-accrual measure: Accruals are [(change in current assets − change in cash and cash equivalents) − (change in current liabilities − change in debt included in current liabilities) − depreciation and amortization expense], scaled by average total assets. The paper’s general rank-scaling statement does not clarify whether this binary indicator is rank-scaled.
independent_variables.formula: C_t = 1 if Accruals_t < 0 and Revision_t > 0, or Accruals_t > 0 and Revision_t < 0; 0 otherwise. Whether C is subsequently portfolio-rank scaled is unclear.

evidence.quote: Specifically, for each of the 10 accrual portfolios we identify firms as having consistent signals when Accruals is negative (positive) and Revision is positive (negative).

An observation is included in the consistent signals subsample if the mean consensus analyst forecast for year t þ 1 is revised upward (downward) in the month of the year t earnings announcement and year t accruals are negative (positive); otherwise it is included in the inconsistent signals subsample.
C is an indicator variable that equals one for firms with accruals and analyst forecast revisions that are consistent in indicating low earnings persistence, and zero otherwise.

Accruals 1⁄4 ðDCA � DCASHÞ � ðDCL � DSTDÞ � DEP, where DCA 1⁄4 change in current assets, DCASH 1⁄4 change in cash/cash equivalents, DCL 1⁄4 change in current liabilities, DSTD 1⁄4 change in debt included in current liabilities, and DEP 1⁄4 depreciation and amortization expense, all scaled by average total assets.
All explanatory variables are scaled portfolio ranks.

research_interest_evidence.quote: C is an indicator variable that equals one for firms with accruals and analyst forecast revisions that are consistent in indicating low earnings persistence, and zero otherwise.
If consistent signals are associated with more or less accurate pricing of accruals than are inconsistent signals, d1C will differ from zero.

independent_variables.research_interest_reason: C is the consistent-signal main-effect indicator; the selected H5 prediction concerns the accrual slope and its interaction with C, while C adjusts the group intercept.

independent_variables.name: RAccruals
independent_variables.definition: Year-t rank of the accrual portfolio, scaled to the zero-to-one range. The ranked quantity is the paper’s total Accruals measure: Accruals are [(change in current assets − change in cash and cash equivalents) − (change in current liabilities − change in debt included in current liabilities) − depreciation and amortization expense], scaled by average total assets.
independent_variables.formula: RAccruals_t = year-t accrual-portfolio rank scaled to [0,1], where Accruals is Accruals_t = [(ΔCA_t − ΔCash_t) − (ΔCL_t − ΔSTD_t) − Dep_t] / average total assets_t, where ΔCA is change in current assets, ΔCash is change in cash/cash equivalents, ΔCL is change in current liabilities, ΔSTD is change in debt included in current liabilities, and Dep is depreciation and amortization expense.

evidence.quote: RAccruals equals the portfolio rank of accruals, scaled to range from zero to one.
RAccruals is the rank of the accrual portfolio in year t, scaled to be between zero and one.

Accruals 1⁄4 ðDCA � DCASHÞ � ðDCL � DSTDÞ � DEP, where DCA 1⁄4 change in current assets, DCASH 1⁄4 change in cash/cash equivalents, DCL 1⁄4 change in current liabilities, DSTD 1⁄4 change in debt included in current liabilities, and DEP 1⁄4 depreciation and amortization expense, all scaled by average total assets.

research_interest_evidence.quote: Based on Sloan (1996), we expect that d1 is negative.
If consistent signals are associated with more or less accurate pricing of accruals than are inconsistent signals, d1C will differ from zero.

independent_variables.research_interest_reason: The accrual portfolio-rank coefficient tests the predicted relation between accruals and future returns.

fixed_effects.details: The paper does not report fixed effects for the selected Equation (3)/Table 4 Panel B regressions.

standard_errors.details: Table 4 reports time-series means and standard deviations of the annual regression coefficients. Significance is based on time-series standard errors of the coefficient means. The paper does not identify a within-annual-regression standard-error correction or clustering method.

evidence.quote: Statistics in boldfaced font are significantly different from zero at less than the 0.05 level, based on time-series standard errors of the means.
Rtþi 1⁄4 d0 þ d0CCt þ d1RAccrualst

estimation_procedure.description: Separate annual cross-sectional regressions are fit for each return horizon i = 1, 2, and 3. Table 4 reports 16 annual fits for t+1, 15 for t+2, and 14 for t+3 and summarizes their coefficients as time-series means and standard deviations. These are counts of fitted annual regressions, not observation N.

evidence.quote: As with all of our tests, i ranges from one to three.
There are 16, 15, and 14 annual regressions when Rtþ1, Rtþ2, and Rtþ3 is the dependent variable, respectively.
Panel B: Regression summary statistics

preprocessing.description: The source states that all explanatory variables are scaled portfolio ranks. The separate Table 4 definition of C specifies a zero/one indicator; the source does not clarify whether C or the constructed C_RAccruals term is rank-scaled after construction.

evidence.quote: All explanatory variables are scaled portfolio ranks.
C is an indicator variable that equals one for firms with accruals and analyst forecast revisions that are consistent in indicating low earnings persistence, and zero otherwise.

scope.quote: Strikingly, a combined strategy that uses forecast revisions to refine the accrual strategy generates a hedge return of 28.5%.
Our primary tests build on prior research that documents market anomalies related to accruals and revisions of analyst earnings forecasts.

To test hypothesis H5 and H5_Alt, regarding the relation between future returns and the accrual component of current earnings, we estimate the relation between the portfolio rank of accruals and future returns.

To ensure that any significant relation between current year accruals and future returns is incremental to other factors identified in prior research as predictors of future returns, we also estimate equation (3):
Table 4, panel B, presents summary statistics from estimating equations (2) and (3).

The next two columns reveal that although the relations between future returns and the control variables generally are consistent with prior research, their inclusion in equation (3) does not affect our inferences relating to RAccruals or C_RAccruals.

equation.quote: Rtþi 1⁄4 d0 þ d0CCt þ d1RAccrualst þ d1CC RAccrualst þ d2 lnMVt þ d3 lnBMt þ d4EPt þ d5Betat þ d6VOLt þ e3tþi
þ d2 ln MVt þ d3 ln BMt þ d4EPt þ d5Betat þ d5VOLt þ e3tþi; ð3Þ

Body Eq(3): R_(t+i) = delta_0 + delta_0C*C_t + delta_1*RAccruals_t + delta_1C*C_RAccruals_t + delta_2*lnMV_t + delta_3*lnBM_t + delta_4*EP_t + delta_5*Beta_t + delta_5*VOL_t + epsilon_(3,t+i). The body repeats delta_5 on Beta and VOL.

sample.quote: The sample comprises all firm years with available data on the Compustat annual industrial and research files and on the CRSP monthly stock returns file for NYSE, AMEX, and NASDAQ firms.

We eliminate firms lacking financial statement data needed to calculate accruals, e.g., financial institutions. We also impose minimum size criteria; we require firms to have sales greater than $25 million, total assets greater than $50 million, and a share price between $1 and $250.
This results in a sample of 24,343 firm-year observations with the required financial statement and returns data; analyst forecast revisions are available for 20,927 of these.
Missing data for other variables results in varying numbers of observations across analyses.
There are 16, 15, and 14 annual regressions when Rtþ1, Rtþ2, and Rtþ3 is the dependent variable, respectively.

missing_fields.method: The selected Table 4 annual regressions are not linked to a named estimator in the paper.
missing_fields.sample_size: Table 4 reports counts of annual fits by return horizon, not observation N within each fit or pooled across fits. The broader 20,927 firm-year analyst-revision sample is not an exact N for Equation (3).
missing_fields.independent_variables[0].definition: C is explicitly defined as a zero/one indicator, while the paper separately says all explanatory variables are portfolio-rank scaled; it does not specify whether the C term is rank-scaled after construction.
missing_fields.independent_variables[2].definition: The source verifies the interaction as C_t × RAccruals_t but does not state whether this constructed term is additionally portfolio-rank scaled under the general statement about explanatory variables.
missing_fields.independent_variables[5].definition: EP is identified only as the earnings-to-price ratio; the paper does not further specify the earnings or price inputs.

review_notes: The body Equation (3) prints δ5 for both Beta and VOL; the selected Table 4 Panel B full-control equation prints δ5 for Beta and δ6 for VOL. The table-specific equation is transcribed; the body/table coefficient-label conflict remains.
The exact annual-regression estimator and per-fit N are unreported. Table 4’s 16, 15, and 14 values are counts of annual fits by horizon, not observations.
Although the construction of C_RAccruals is verified as multiplication, it remains unclear whether the authors applied their general portfolio-rank scaling to C or to the product interaction.
results_review_notes: Table 4 Panel B reports means and standard deviations across annual coefficient fits. The mean is stored as the reported estimate and each parenthetical SD is stored in reported_distribution, not as a standard error. Boldface identifies only p<0.05 based on time-series SEs of coefficient means; no t/z statistic, exact p-value, reference distribution, or degrees of freedom is reported. Counts of annual fits are not observation Ns. Adjusted R-squared is excluded as a model-fit quantity.

review_notes: Selected the full-control Equation (3) return-predictability family in Table 4 Panel B. The paper’s central contribution concerns how analyst forecast revisions refine the accrual pricing signal; Equation (3) is the final full-control regression of future returns on the accrual rank, consistent-signal indicator and interaction, and return predictors. Equation (2) is the reduced-control version and is excluded under the full-control rule. Equation (1) tests the antecedent forecast-revision/persistence relation; Equations (4)–(5) are later persistence analyses, outside this selected pricing family.

The body Equation (3) on physical page 9 prints δ5 for both Beta and VOL, while the Table 4 Panel B selected equation on physical page 20 prints δ5 for Beta and δ6 for VOL. The RHS terms are all identifiable; the selected model follows the full-control table equation and preserves this coefficient-label discrepancy for review.

The supplied checked transcription confirms C_RAccruals = C × RAccruals. The paper defines C as a zero/one indicator and separately says all explanatory variables are scaled portfolio ranks, but does not clarify whether the binary C or the interaction is rank-scaled.

The underlying estimator for the annual regressions is not named. Table 4 reports 16, 15, and 14 annual fits at horizons t+1, t+2, and t+3, but not an exact observation count for any fit; sample_size is therefore null.

evidence.quote: analyst forecast revisions are available for 20,927 of these.

Revision is the mean consensus analyst forecast for year t þ 1 earnings outstanding at the end of the month of the year t earnings announcement minus the mean consensus analyst forecast for year t þ 1 outstanding at the end of the month preceding the year t earnings announcement.

Accruals 1⁄4 ðDCA � DCASHÞ � ðDCL � DSTDÞ � DEP, where DCA 1⁄4 change in current assets, DCASH 1⁄4 change in cash/cash equivalents, DCL 1⁄4 change in current liabilities, DSTD 1⁄4 change in debt included in current liabilities, and DEP 1⁄4 depreciation and amortization expense, all scaled by average total assets.
